chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

While Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was among a gathering of his companions, a man came to him and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed penetration with a boy, so purify me.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “O this one, go to your home; perhaps a black bile episode has been stirred in you.” Then when it was the next day, he returned to him and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed penetration with a boy, so purify me.” He said to him: “O this one, go to your home; perhaps a black bile episode has been stirred in you.” He did that three times after his first time.

Then when it was the fourth time, he said to him: “O this one, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ruled in the case of one like you with three rulings, so choose whichever of them you wish.” He said: “And what are they, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn?” He said: “A strike with the sword upon your neck, reaching whatever it reaches; or casting you down from a mountain while your hands and feet are bound; or burning with fire.” He said to him: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, which of them is most severe upon me?” He said: “Burning with fire.” He said: “Then I have chosen it, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn.” He said: “Then prepare yourself for that.”

He said: “Yes.” Then he performed two rakʿahs, then sat in his tashahhud and said: “O Allah, I have committed of sin what You already know, and I have feared because of that, so I came to the legatee of Your Messenger and the cousin of Your Prophet, and I asked him to purify me. So he gave me the choice between three kinds of punishment, and I have chosen the most severe of them. O Allah, I ask You to make that an expiation for my sins, and not to burn me with Your Fire in my Hereafter.”

Then he stood while weeping until he sat in the pit that Amīr al-Muʾminīn had dug for him, while he saw the fire blazing around him. He said: Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام wept, and all his companions wept, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “Rise, O this one, for you have made the angels of heaven and the angels of earth weep, and Allah has indeed accepted your repentance. So rise, and do not ever return to anything of what you had done.”

key_terms.أَحْكَامٍ: rulings; the legal punishments mentioned for this offense.
key_terms.أَوْقَبْتُ: I committed anal penetration; a legal term used here in confessing the act of liwat.
key_terms.الْإِحْرَاقُ بِالنَّارِ: burning with fire; the severest of the punishments mentioned in the report.
key_terms.تَابَ عَلَيْكَ: He has accepted your repentance; a declaration of divine acceptance of tawbah.
key_terms.فَطَهِّرْنِي: purify me; meaning to purify me through the prescribed legal consequence.
key_terms.كَفَّارَةً: expiation; that which wipes away the burden of sins.
key_terms.وَصِيِّ رَسُولِكَ: the legatee of Your Messenger; referring to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith portray the relationship between legal punishment and sincere repentance in the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a man’s repeated confession before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding a grave sexual sin and his request for purification through legal punishment. It highlights both the severity of the offense in legal terms and the transformative force of sincere tawbah, culminating in divine acceptance of repentance before the punishment was carried out.
